question: What will be the last date for filing claims and objections in Delhi's SIR, as of November 27, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is Nov 25, but a fresh Annexure-A door-to-door round for ~47.5 lakh ASDD electors (ECI letter Nov 6) had not begun as of Nov 16, with distribution expected 'later this week'; that cannot finish by Nov 25. The Tribune (Nov 13) reports a ~2-week extension under consideration, and ThePrint (Nov 16) quotes officials saying another extension is likely. The SC hears the case Nov 19 and has said it could direct an extension. Reference class: the two prior Delhi SIR claims extensions (30 and 26 days, each notified 1-4 days before the deadline). A ~2-week extension gives ~Dec 9 (Dec 5-15 bucket); a repeat of the ~month-long pattern or an SC push gives Dec 16+. Main downside risk: the ECI extends only the Annexure-A window without moving the claims date, which the fine print excludes. Market check: none found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold; my own search found nothing; Kalshi/bookmakers not separately searched).
calls.dossier:
- Status quo: last date for claims/objections = Nov 25, 2026 (ECI notif. 23/2026-ERS dated Oct 29; ThePrint report on the Oct 29 revision); disposal Dec 15; final roll Dec 22.
- Prior extensions: Sep 30 -> Oct 30 (ECI/PN/120/2026, Sep 26; +30 days); Oct 30 -> Nov 25 (Oct 29 notif; +26 days, a day after the SC asked the ECI to consider extending). Both were notified 1-4 days before the deadline in force.
- ECI letter of Nov 6, 2026 to the CEOs of Delhi + 6 states: ASDD-omitted electors may submit Annexure-A enumeration forms during the ongoing SIR; no separate closing date found (Outlook, Scroll).
- The Tribune (Nov 13): ECI considering extending the Delhi SIR by 'around two weeks'; ~15,000 BLOs to revisit addresses of ~47.6 lakh excluded voters; 'will be taken up in next meeting and finalised'; not yet approved.
- TMV (Nov 14): fresh form distribution expected 'in full swing next week'; ECINET being modified so BLOs can generate forms for excluded voters.
- ThePrint (Nov 16): 31,027 Form 6 applications received Oct 29 - Nov 15 (total ~3.10 lakh since Aug 31); officials say 'the SIR exercise may see another extension'; fresh form distribution 'expected to begin later this week'.
- SC: Delhi SIR Form 6 matter listed Nov 19, 2026; CJI said the court could consider directing the ECI to extend the deadline if necessary (Deccan Chronicle / Deccan Herald / LiveLaw).
- Comparison: in Maharashtra the claims deadline was extended Oct 26 -> Nov 13 with final roll Nov 30; whether the Nov 6 Annexure-A letter caused further claims extensions in the other 6 states was not found.
- Fine-print risk: an extension limited to Annexure-A distribution/submission or house-to-house verification does NOT count; only a change to the claims/objections last date counts (Form 6 governs if dates split).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off ECI/CEO Delhi notifications, press notes, or Delhi Gazette dated on or before Nov 27, 2026, not off media speculation.
- Event window: now (Nov 17) -> Nov 27, 2026 23:59 IST; a revision must be dated within that span; as of Nov 17 roughly 0% of the 10-day remaining window has elapsed, and the Nov 25 deadline is 8 days away.
- Searched but not found: any official notification after Oct 29; the outcome of the CEO Delhi timeline review; prediction markets (none found on Polymarket/Manifold).

calls.dossier:
- Baseline: ECI notification 23/2026-ERS dated Oct 29, 2026 set the claims/objections last date at Nov 25, disposal by Dec 15 and the final roll on Dec 22 (ThePrint, Outlook, DD News, Oct 29-30). The previous date was Oct 30 (26-day extension); before that it was Sep 30 (30-day extension, PN of Sep 26).
- Oct 29 revision came the day after the SC asked the ECI to consider extending (ThePrint, Oct 29). The same batch moved Maharashtra's claims deadline to Nov 13 (final roll Nov 30) and extended the AP, Haryana, Telangana and Nagaland processing periods.
- Nov 4: SC listed the Delhi Form 6 dispute for Nov 19; the CJI said the bench could ask the ECI to extend the deadline if necessary (ThePrint/ETV, Nov 4).
- Nov 6: ECI directed the CEOs of Delhi and six states to accept Annexure-A enumeration forms from excluded voters, with fresh door-to-door verification. ECINET is being modified to generate the forms (ThePrint, Daily Excelsior).
- Nov 13 (The Tribune): ECI considering extending the Delhi SIR by about two weeks; 'will be taken up for discussion in the next meeting and finalised'; not approved. 15,000 BLOs will distribute forms.
- Nov 13 (The Patriot): distribution not yet begun at scale; expected from the following week.
- Nov 16 (ThePrint): 31,027 Form 6 applications Oct 29-Nov 15 (~3.10 lakh total). Officials say 'the SIR exercise may see another extension'; fresh form distribution expected later that week.
- Nov 16 (Indian Opinion): in Maharashtra, enumeration forms not yet generated via ECINET 10 days after the ECI order; officials say 'no deadline has been set for the exercise' and the final roll (Nov 30) will likely be delayed. No formal extension of Maharashtra's Nov 13 claims date found.
- Nov 16 was a Delhi public holiday (Chhath).
- Status quo: Nov 25 last date unless a revision dated on or before Nov 27 is issued.
- Resolution note: resolves off ECI/CEO Delhi notifications or press notes or the Delhi Gazette dated on or before Nov 27. Extending only the Annexure-A distribution/verification or the disposal date does NOT count; the Form 6 last date governs. An extension with no closing date resolves to Dec 16 or later.
- Event window: Oct 29 -> Nov 27, 2026 (23:59 IST) per the criteria; as of Nov 17, ~67% elapsed (10 days remain).
- Historical pattern: both earlier Delhi extensions were notified 1-4 days before the deadline then in force.
- Searched but not found: any official notice dated after Oct 29 changing the Delhi date; the outcome of the Nov 19 SC hearing (not yet held); a formal extension of Maharashtra's Nov 13 claims deadline; any prediction market.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts and differ only in weighting. Two factual points remain unsettled offline: (1) Run 2's claim that Maharashtra's Nov 13 claims date passed without formal extension, which no run contradicts; I treat it as moderately credible evidence that the ECI separates the Annexure-A process from the claims window, and it supports 20-22% on no extension rather than Run 1's 15%. (2) Whether Tribune's 'two weeks' refers to the claims date or to the overall schedule; unresolved, so it is spread between the Dec 5-15 bucket and the no-extension/scope-limited outcome. I agree with the runs' reference class. The modal bucket is Dec 5-15, with a substantial tail for a repeat of the month-long pattern or an SC-driven or open-ended extension.
